metadata.methodology: PASS only on a matching static reject diagnostic or a matching runtime trap message; safe control PASS only on a clean build+run. DEFAULT unsanitized is WARN-only by design (exact C+ warning -> WARN_ONLY). Documented static/sanitizer gaps -> KNOWN_OPEN; provable-constant cases with no native guard -> STATIC_ONLY_BY_DESIGN. Compilation alone is never proof. Timeouts are FAIL.

cases.why: docs/LIMITATIONS.md bug 1: a provable constant subscript is a static error; dynamic cases must trap via __cplus_bounds_check/ASan.
docs/LIMITATIONS.md bug 1: flow-sensitive branch index is provable in check; otherwise the runtime bounds check must trap.
docs/LIMITATIONS.md bug 1: known allocation extent is checked statically; otherwise ASan/bounds check must trap.
docs/LIMITATIONS.md bug 2: named single-TU UAF shapes are rejected; other shapes need ASan/allocation side table.
docs/LIMITATIONS.md bug 5: direct double release is rejected statically; allocator side table/ASan is the runtime backstop.
docs/LIMITATIONS.md bug 6 and docs/SAFE_MODE_SPEC.md: provable null is rejected; DEFAULT warning is WARN_ONLY, and unsanitized builds must trap with a diagnostic (a bare SIGSEGV is not evidence).

docs/ARITHMETIC_SAFETY.md section 1 and the pinned arith_shift_negative/arith_shift_wide native diagnostics: C+ deliberately treats a volatile local's initializer as a conservative compile-time fact, so STRICT rejects 'signed integer overflow in addition' and DEFAULT warns exactly. No native runtime guard is emitted for this provable constant (docs/LIMITATIONS.md bug 9); DEBUG/RELEASE record STATIC_ONLY_BY_DESIGN, not a defect.

docs/ARITHMETIC_SAFETY.md section 3: a provably zero divisor is a static finding (STRICT error / DEFAULT warning), and C+ deliberately emits no native guard for constants. DEBUG/RELEASE record STATIC_ONLY_BY_DESIGN with the exact warning; runtime-variable division is covered by div_zero_runtime (rc 110).

docs/ARITHMETIC_SAFETY.md section 8 and docs/LIMITATIONS.md bug 25: a divisor that is not provably zero is rejected in STRICT / warned in DEFAULT and the native guard traps rc 110 ('C+ runtime error: division by zero: division by zero').
docs/LIMITATIONS.md bug 19 and docs/ARITHMETIC_SAFETY.md section 8: shift count is a static check with a native rc 110 guard.

docs/compiler/adversarial-wave2.md section 'The three still accepted by check': A1_implicit_narrow is accepted by check but build --strict --sanitize=none traps rc 111. This toolchain's --sanitize=address,undefined has no implicit-truncation check (observed rc 44), so sanitizer configs are KNOWN_OPEN; native build configs still require the trap.

docs/compiler/adversarial-wave2.md section 'The three still accepted by check': A1_float_to_int is accepted by check but the build traps rc 111; UBSan float-cast-overflow also proves it in sanitizer configs.
docs/LIMITATIONS.md bug 7: -Werror=uninitialized rejects this case in every config; MemorySanitizer would be the runtime-only fallback but is not enabled here.
